APPROACH 1: TF-IDF as a vectorizer
```{r}
# https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/textrecipes/versions/0.2.3
# https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/textrecipes/textrecipes.pdf

# First, we create the recipe to clean and transform tweets into vectors 

recipe_1 <- recipe(Party ~ Tweet, data = tweets_train) %>% 
  step_text_normalization(Tweet) %>% # text standartization
  step_tokenize(Tweet) %>% # splitting text into tokens              
  step_stopwords(Tweet) %>%  # deleting stopwords (useless ones)          
  step_stem(Tweet) %>% # stemmatization = only roots from words     
  step_tokenfilter(Tweet, min_times = 20, max_tokens=500) %>% # removing noise + preventing RAM explosion
  # WHY? ->  https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/textrecipes/textrecipes.pdf -> based on this article:  step_tokenfilter is a good strategy is to start with a low token count and go up according to how much RAM you want to use.
  # It is strongly advised to filter before using step_tf or step_tfidf to limit the number of variables created.
  step_tfidf(Tweet) # tf-idf as a method of vectorization
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# preparing and applying recipe

rec1_prep <- prep(recipe_1, training = tweets_train)

train_tweets1 <- bake(rec1_prep, new_data = tweets_train)

# Before training the models, we build logistic regressions using the formulas we included in the recipes, as we've done in HW-3

model_glm <- glm(Party ~ ., data = train_tweets1, family = "binomial") # logistic regression model with two classes (Republican / Democrat)
```


```{r}
test_tweets1  <- bake(rec1_prep, new_data = tweets_test)

# prediction
pred_train_1 <- predict(model_glm, newdata = train_tweets1, type = "response")
pred_test_1 <- predict(model_glm, newdata = test_tweets1, type = "response")
```

```{r}
# converting probabilities to class labels BECAUSE of these errors -> 
pred_train_1 <- ifelse(pred_train_1 > 0.5, 1, 0) # Error in confusionMatrix.default(data = relevel(pred_train_1, ref = "1"),  : the data cannot have more levels than the reference
pred_train_1 <- as.factor(pred_train_1) # Error in relevel.default(pred_train_1, ref = "1") : 'relevel' only for (unordered) factors
```

```{r}
summary(model_glm)
# In general, people who use words such as: access, afford, bring, children, class, clear, cost are more likely to be Democrats
# While words (back, bill, benefit, border, business, capital) are associated with Republicans. 
```

```{r}
cv1 <- train(
  recipe_1,
  data = tweets_train,
  method = "glm",
  family = "binomial",
  trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", number = 3) # only 3-fold cv because otherwise training was way too long 
)
```

```{r}
# extracting probabilities 
m1_prob_train <- predict(cv1, tweets_train, type = "prob")$"1"
m1_prob_test <- predict(cv1, tweets_test, type="prob")$"1"
```

```{r}
# ROC curve 
perf1_train <- prediction(m1_prob_train, tweets_train$Party) %>% 
  performance(measure = "tpr", x.measure = "fpr")

# plotting performance
plot(perf1_train, col = "black")

# In terms of FPR and TPR, the model is much better than a random model. However of course, it is not perfect classifiers (0,1). 
```


APPROACH 2:  Embeddings implementation
```{r}
library(word2vec)
```

We will need a custom function for correct execution -->
```{r}
# referencees: 
# https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/word2vec/versions/0.4.0/topics/word2vec
# https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/word2vec/versions/0.4.0/topics/word2vec
# https://pub.towardsai.net/unlocking-the-potential-of-text-a-closer-look-at-pre-embedding-cleaning-methods-7c44f2d4ec60

get_embeddings <- function(texts, dim = 30) {
  
  # Basic text cleaning
  clean_texts <- sapply(texts, function(x) {
    if(is.na(x) || nchar(x) == 0) return("")
    # Removing non-ASCII characters
    x <- iconv(x, to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT", sub = "")
    # Removing URLs, mentions, hashtags
    x <- gsub("http\\S+\\s*", "", x)
    x <- gsub("@\\w+", "", x)
    x <- gsub("#\\w+", "", x)
    # Removing punctuation and digits
    x <- gsub("[^a-zA-Z\\s]", " ", x)
    # Converting to lowercase and trim
    x <- tolower(trimws(x))
    return(x)
  })
  
  # Removing empty texts and track valid indices
  non_empty <- nchar(clean_texts) > 0
  clean_texts <- clean_texts[non_empty]
  valid_indices <- which(non_empty)
  
  if(length(clean_texts) == 0) {
    return(list(embeddings = matrix(0, nrow = 0, ncol = dim), 
                valid_indices = integer(0)))
  }
  
  # Writing to temporary file for word2vec
  temp_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
  writeLines(clean_texts, temp_file, useBytes = TRUE)
  
  # Training word2vec model
  model <- word2vec(temp_file, type = "cbow", dim = dim, iter = 5)
  
  # Cleaning up
  unlink(temp_file)
  
  # Getting embeddings
  word_vectors <- as.matrix(model)
  
  # Creating document embeddings
  tokens <- strsplit(clean_texts, "\\s+")
  doc_embeddings <- t(sapply(tokens, function(doc_words) {
    valid_words <- doc_words[doc_words %in% rownames(word_vectors)]
    if(length(valid_words) > 0) {
      colMeans(word_vectors[valid_words, , drop = FALSE])
    } else {
      rep(0, ncol(word_vectors))
    }
  }))
  
  return(list(embeddings = doc_embeddings, valid_indices = valid_indices))
}
```

```{r}
# Applying word2vec to our data (generating word2vec embeddings)
set.seed(123)

train_result <- get_embeddings(tweets_train$Tweet, dim = 30)
test_result <- get_embeddings(tweets_test$Tweet, dim = 30)
```

```{r}
# Converting to data frames with proper Party assignment
train_embeddings_df <- as.data.frame(train_result$embeddings)
colnames(train_embeddings_df) <- paste0("V", 1:ncol(train_embeddings_df))
```

```{r}
# Using valid indices to align Party labels correctly
train_embeddings_df$Party <- tweets_train$Party[train_result$valid_indices]
test_embeddings_df <- as.data.frame(test_result$embeddings)

colnames(test_embeddings_df) <- paste0("V", 1:ncol(test_embeddings_df))
test_embeddings_df$Party <- tweets_test$Party[test_result$valid_indices]
```

```{r}
# Training model on embeddings
model_glm_embeddings <- glm(Party ~ ., data = train_embeddings_df, family = "binomial")
```

```{r}
# Making predictions
pred_train_embeddings <- predict(model_glm_embeddings, newdata = train_embeddings_df, type = "response")
pred_test_embeddings <- predict(model_glm_embeddings, newdata = test_embeddings_df, type = "response")

pred_train_embeddings_factor <- as.factor(ifelse(pred_train_embeddings > 0.5, 1, 0))
pred_test_embeddings_factor <- as.factor(ifelse(pred_test_embeddings > 0.5, 1, 0))
```


Model evaluation --> accuracy 0.59 on train and 0.52 on test
```{r}
confusionMatrix(
  data = relevel(pred_train_embeddings_factor, ref = "1"),
  reference = relevel(train_embeddings_df$Party, ref = "1")
)

```

```{r}
confusionMatrix(
  data = relevel(pred_test_embeddings_factor, ref = "1"),
  reference = relevel(test_embeddings_df$Party, ref = "1")
) 
```
